title: Runtime Output Sanity Agent: real-time function-call compatibility checks and auto-revert policy
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Build a lightweight runtime agent ("Sanity Agent") that runs alongside model variants during canary/A-B/shadow rollouts to detect structured-output and function-call incompatibilities in near-real time and initiate automated mitigations (soft-block, traffic reroute, or auto-revert). The agent should provide low-overhead diffing of output shapes, signature mismatches for function-calls, and a small hierarchy of severity levels to inform rollback decisions. This ticket scopes the minimum viable checks, deployment strategy for Dedicated/Hosted, and the initial ops UI hooks for manual override.
acceptance_criteria: Sanity Agent deployed as a sidecar in the serving runtime such that it can observe request/response pairs for canary and shadow traffic with <5% added latency at p95 for standard prompt sizes

Detects three classes of incompatibility: (1) function signature mismatch (name or params), (2) missing/extra required fields in structured output, (3) major type changes (e.g., string -> array) and emits a normalized diff event
Diff event schema published to the console events stream and tagged with severity (info/warn/error) and confidence score

Automatic mitigation policy implemented: on error-severity breaches above configured threshold (default: 1% of requests or 50 errors in 10m), traffic is re-routed to baseline model and an auto-revert action is logged
Ops console displays recent diffs with example payloads, confidence heuristics, and one-click rollback/ignore controls
End-to-end tests covering deterministic and stochastic function-call outputs, and a performance benchmark validating overhead criteria
design_decisions: Run agent as a sidecar process instead of inline to simplify rollback and reduce blast radius
Use a two-layer diff: lightweight signature checks for every request and optional deep schema validation sampled at 1% to control cost
Represent function-call compatibility as: function_id + ordered param schema + required/optional flags, and compute a canonical fingerprint for fast compatibility checks
Classify incompatibilities into severity tiers: INFO (cosmetic), WARN (possible regression), ERROR (likely breaking change) — only ERROR triggers automated reroute by default
Avoid blocking production traffic; agent only triggers routing changes via control-plane signals to maintain consistent serving paths and auditability
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Prototyping (2w) - implement sidecar shim that captures outputs, computes fingerprints, and emits diffs to a local buffer
Phase 2: Sampling + Deep Validator (2w) - add sampled JSON Schema validation and function-call argument type checks; add confidence heuristics for nondeterministic outputs
Phase 3: Control-plane integration (1w) - implement mitigation API to signal traffic re-route and record audit events
Phase 4: Console + Alerts (1w) - surface diffs in Console, add alerting rule and one-click rollback button
Phase 5: Canary rollout + internal dogfood (1w) - run against internal models and iterate on thresholds and sampling rates
testing_plan: Unit tests for fingerprinting, diffing heuristics, and severity classification
Integration tests that inject synthetic function-call schema drifts and verify mitigation triggers
Load test in staging using replayed production traffic (10M tokens) to ensure <5% latency overhead at p95
Fuzz tests for malformed/edge-case structured outputs to ensure agent is resilient and fails open (does not block traffic)
Run a 48-hour A/B with internal customers and collect false-positive/false-negative metrics
comments: 2025-11-03 Aisha Kumar: Initial write-up and proposal. Spikes show that simple signature hashing is <1ms per request in Go; deep JSON Schema validation costs ~2-6ms — will sample.

2025-11-04 Liam Chen: Reviewing trade-offs. Concern: noisy auto-reverts for models that intentionally change optional fields. Proposal: add per-model allowlist of tolerant fields and a learning phase that seeds allowlist from golden prompts.

2025-11-05 Product review (Marta Silva): We need a clear customer-facing SLA for auto-reverts and an audit trail for compliance. Add requirement to persist diff evidence for 30 days for enterprise customers.
2025-11-06 Security (Rahul Patel): Sidecar must not persist PII. Agent will strip/obfuscate user data in diffs and mark evidence as redacted. Will require architecture review before release.
2025-11-06 Liam Chen: Updated estimate to 8 pts and set security_review_required=true. Next actions: spike sampling config and prototype sidecar shim in runtime branch.
